name: Training needs analysis
summary: For one team, the HR lead or team manager gets what each role must be able to do, how many people can do it now, where the team falls short, and the training to arrange first, with who arranges it and by when. Counted by role, never a rating of a named person.

sources.title: Fully Powered AI's own rules for prepared work and the counted form of this one: the manager's two lists as the only authority, stated column headers with a stop when one does not match, counts per role and never names, every gap written as a question for the approver, prices only as supplied, and nothing booked, bought, sent or recorded until a person decides.

sources.contribution: Working from named roles rather than everyone; a grid of roles against required abilities on a level scale, with the source behind each current level; the shortfall as required less held; an ability held by one person marked by role, not by name; certificate end dates tracked; an owner and a date on every action.

How much ability a role needs follows from the work it does, not from whoever holds the role today; a renewal date set ahead of each certificate's expiry; requirements set by a rule ranked first; and training treated as one remedy among others, never the only answer to every shortfall.
Requirements sorted by how much they matter, and the remedy matched to the kind of gap: someone who has learned a thing but lacks the chance to do it needs practice, not a course.
